script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. RURAL ROAD - DAY

A country road. Cars pass by occasionally. We hear the soft sound of crickets and birds. A SCHOOL BUS approaches. The door opens. CHILDREN file out.

INT. SCHOOL BUS - DAY

MRS. WEST, a kindly, middle-aged bus driver, checks the aisle for stragglers. She sees a young boy, JIM, lingering. She smiles.

MRS. WEST
(cheerfully)
Jimmy, are you all set?

JIM
(shrugs)
I guess.

MRS. WEST
(gently)
Well, you know where to find me if you need anything.

Jim nods and exits the bus. Mrs. West watches him go, a worried expression on her face.

EXT. TOWN - DAY

The children scatter, their laughter ringing through the air. Jim walks alone, a sad look on his face. He passes a DILAPIDATED HOUSE where an old man, MR. JENKINS, sits in a rocking chair.

MR. JENKINS
(calling)
Jimmy! Come here, boy.

Jim hesitates, then approaches.

MR. JENKINS
(smiling)
Another day of learning, huh? How was it?

JIM
(sighs)
The same.

MR. JENKINS
(nodding)
Well, it's not easy, is it? But you'll make it through.

INT. JIM'S HOUSE - NIGHT

Jim sits at the kitchen table, staring at his homework. His mother, MARY, enters, looking weary.

MARY
(exhausted)
You still up?

JIM
(nods)
I can't do this, Mom. I don't understand any of it.

MARY
(sighs)
You'll figure it out, Jim. I believe in you.

INT. MR. JENKINS' HOUSE - DAY

Jim visits Mr. Jenkins, who shows him an old photo album.

MR. JENKINS
(gesturing)
See this, Jimmy? This is me when I was your age. I was just like you. But I made it through. And so will you.

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

Jim struggles in class, but perseveres. He sits next to a quiet girl, LUCY, who offers him encouragement and help.

LUCY
(smiling)
You can do it, Jim.

INT. LIBRARY - NIGHT

Jim and Lucy study together, their friendship growing. They discuss their dreams and aspirations.

JIM
I want to be a writer.

LUCY
(excitedly)
That's wonderful, Jim! What will you write about?

JIM
(thoughtful)
I don't know yet. But I'll figure it out.

INT. FAIRGROUNDS - DAY

The town's annual fair. Jim and Lucy enter a writing contest. They work together on a story.

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

The results are announced. Jim and Lucy have won the contest. The entire class cheers for them.

MR. JENKINS
(beaming)
I knew you could do it, Jimmy.

Jim smiles, feeling a newfound sense of pride and accomplishment.

FADE OUT.

THE END
